tests.title: Live video continuity
tests.measures: Drives a synthetic stream through the real ingest path (file capture + percept.run) and checks monotonic timestamps, zero reordering, and that every injected sequence gap is accounted for by a typed discontinuity with an exact missing count.
notes: SourceTracker keeps only the LAST accepted (epoch, sequence) per stream, so only an exact redelivery of that sequence is typed source_duplicate; an earlier sequence arriving late is typed source_reorder (percept/runtime/envelope.py:459-462). Both are excluded without advancing state and neither is booked as a missing sequence, so the accounting is exact — but a consumer that wants a true duplicate/late split cannot get it from the event name.

tests.title: Backpressure policy
tests.measures: Stalls the consumer and checks both source queue policies: 'latest' must evict the OLDEST and count every eviction while memory stays bounded; 'block' on a finite fixture must backpressure losslessly.
tests.pass_bar: fixture ('block') path drops exactly zero; live ('latest') path bounded with every drop counted
notes: MEASURED: under a saturated consumer the 'latest' policy cost 104 ms of CAPTURE-THREAD stall per eviction (40 frames took 3.75 s -> 10.7 effective fps). percept/runtime/source.py:77 puts with timeout=0.1 and only evicts on the resulting queue.Full, so the drop trigger is 'full for 100 ms', not 'full'. Memory stays bounded and every queue-level drop IS counted, so the SV-0.2 bar holds — but on a live 30 fps camera this throttles cap.read() to ~10 Hz under backpressure, and frames the driver discards while the capture thread is parked are invisible to the `dropped` counter.

MEASURED (corollary): with a 50 ms/frame consumer — slower than the producer but faster than the 100 ms put timeout — queue_policy='latest' evicted NOTHING and delivered the entire 20-frame backlog in arrival order over 1.03 s. Below the timeout the freshness policy is inert: the consumer receives the oldest queued frame, which is the opposite of the documented 'live streams prefer fresh evidence over stale backlog' (percept/runtime/source.py:51).

percept.run()/_run_worker exposes source_queue_size but NOT queue_policy, so the lossless 'block' mode is unreachable from the public front door — a finite-file replay through percept.run() always uses drop-oldest 'latest'. (percept/runtime/worker.py:4301 builds source_kwargs without queue_policy; percept/runtime/source.py:302 defaults it to 'latest'.) Drops are still counted in RuntimeStats.frames_dropped, so this is lossy-but-honest, not silent.

tests.title: Audio unit ordering
tests.measures: Streams a synthetic wav through the real audio capture adapter, then normalizes and pushes every unit into a real AudioWindow. Checks contiguity, ordering, stamping, byte-exact PCM normalization, and total sample conservation.
tests.pass_bar: zero reordering, zero unaccounted sample loss

tests.title: Fused A/V skew
tests.measures: Injects +/-50, 100, 250 and 500 ms of relative A/V skew plus a mid-stream discontinuity, and compares the synchronizer's reported actual_skew_s and typed coverage uncertainty against an independently computed oracle.
tests.pass_bar: skew always classified; no silent pairing beyond declared tolerance
notes: actual_skew_s is the distance from the video anchor to the NEAREST audio unit, not a systematic lip-sync offset: a uniformly shifted but still-overlapping audio lane reports 0.0 by design (percept/fused_sync.py:611 _skew). Coverage, not offset, is what the synchronizer polices — audio that fails to cover [anchor-window, anchor-max_skew] is typed MISSING_AUDIO (percept/fused_sync.py:788).

tests.title: Delivered-fps honesty
tests.measures: Runs the real capture loop against a source that REPORTS 30 fps while delivering 15, and measures whether/when the rolling-window heuristic emits fps_misreported.
tests.pass_bar: a 30-reported / 15-delivered source is flagged within the 2.0 s window

tests.title: Clock authority
tests.measures: Checks that every envelope carries observation time independently of media time, that exactly one clock is authoritative for the selected timebase, and that decoder source time appears ONLY when the decoder truly provides it.
tests.pass_bar: exactly one authoritative clock per envelope; source_time never manufactured
